<a id="exchange"></a><a id="package-exchange"></a>

## Package exchange

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/exchange"`

Package exchange exchanges an identity provider's access token for a limes capability, by OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693), as docs/adr/0003-oauth-token-exchange.md decides.

An MCP server, or a gateway in front of one, receives the access token its clients got from their authorization server, and exchanges it on its own side for a capability: for its tool calls, and for the agents and services it calls on. Clients keep the OAuth flow they know; the capability carries the operations, resources, budgets and revocation the access token does not.

An Exchanger does it in process. A Handler serves it as an RFC 8693 token endpoint, for a gateway or a token service within one trust domain. What each exchange grants is the Policy's: there is none by default. The Exchanger holds every answer to the request: the capability's audience is drawn from the resources and audiences asked for, it ends no later than the subject token, a subject token is accepted only from the client it was issued to, and a DPoP proof binds the capability to the client's key (RFC 9449 §5). Config.Exchanges issues one capability per subject token, for a service that exchanges where it receives the token (docs/adr/0009-one-capability-per-subject-token.md).

Subject tokens are verified by a SubjectVerifier. exchange/jwtverify's verifies JWT access tokens (RFC 9068) through jwx; a consumer with a JOSE stack of its own implements SubjectVerifier on it instead, and this package links no JOSE library (docs/adr/0010-exchange-jose-subpackage.md).

Every refusal is an RFC 6749 §5.2 error: [ErrorOf](#exchange.ErrorOf) gives the status and code the Handler answers with, for a consumer that calls an Exchanger in process, and [ErrorCodes](#exchange.ErrorCodes) lists them.

<a id="exchange.ErrInvalidRequest"></a><a id="exchange.ErrInvalidClient"></a><a id="exchange.ErrUnauthorizedClient"></a><a id="exchange.ErrServerError"></a><a id="exchange.ErrInvalidGrant"></a><a id="exchange.ErrInvalidTarget"></a><a id="exchange.ErrTargetExchanged"></a><a id="exchange.ErrInvalidScope"></a><a id="exchange.ErrInvalidAuthorizationDetails"></a><a id="exchange.ErrUnsupportedGrantType"></a>

### exchange.ErrInvalidRequest, exchange.ErrInvalidClient, exchange.ErrUnauthorizedClient, exchange.ErrServerError, exchange.ErrInvalidGrant, exchange.ErrInvalidTarget, exchange.ErrTargetExchanged, exchange.ErrInvalidScope, exchange.ErrInvalidAuthorizationDetails, exchange.ErrUnsupportedGrantType

```go
var (
	// ErrInvalidRequest is a request missing a parameter or malformed.
	ErrInvalidRequest error = &codedError{"exchange: invalid request", limes.CodeInvalidRequest, http.StatusBadRequest, "The request is invalid", limes.CategoryInvalid}
	// ErrInvalidClient is a client the endpoint could not authenticate.
	ErrInvalidClient error = &codedError{"exchange: client not authenticated", limes.CodeInvalidClient, http.StatusUnauthorized, "The client is not authenticated", limes.CategoryUnauthenticated}
	// ErrUnauthorizedClient is a client the endpoint authenticated that may
	// not use it. HandlerConfig.Authenticate and
	// IntrospectionConfig.Authenticate return it, wrapped or not, to refuse
	// such a client.
	ErrUnauthorizedClient error = &codedError{"exchange: client not authorized to exchange", limes.CodeUnauthorizedClient, http.StatusBadRequest, "The client may not exchange tokens", limes.CategoryDenied}
	// ErrServerError is the server failing to decide on a request: its
	// client store unreachable, the issuer or a store failing, the policy
	// erring. HandlerConfig.Authenticate and
	// IntrospectionConfig.Authenticate return it, wrapped or not, so that
	// the endpoint answers 500 server_error, logged at ERROR, rather than
	// tell the client its credentials are wrong (RFC 6749 §5.2). Every
	// error Exchange and Narrow return that is no refusal wraps it, the
	// cause kept in its chain.
	ErrServerError error = &codedError{"exchange: server error", limes.CodeServerError, http.StatusInternalServerError, "The server could not decide on the request", limes.CategoryInternal}
	// ErrInvalidGrant is a subject token refused: not genuine, expired, or
	// not one the client may present.
	ErrInvalidGrant error = &codedError{"exchange: subject token refused", limes.CodeInvalidGrant, http.StatusBadRequest, "The subject token was refused", limes.CategoryUnauthenticated}
	// ErrInvalidTarget is a resource or audience the exchange will not
	// issue for.
	ErrInvalidTarget error = &codedError{"exchange: target refused", limes.CodeInvalidTarget, http.StatusBadRequest, "The resource or audience was refused", limes.CategoryDenied}
	// ErrTargetExchanged is an ErrInvalidTarget of its own: under
	// Config.Exchanges' one capability per subject token, a token
	// exchanged already for other resources or audiences, whose capability
	// a second exchange cannot widen or narrow. The client is told so
	// rather than the target refused, and exchanges the token for its first
	// targets, or another token.
	ErrTargetExchanged = fmt.Errorf("%w: the subject token was exchanged already for other targets", ErrInvalidTarget)
	// ErrInvalidScope is a scope the exchange will not grant.
	ErrInvalidScope error = &codedError{"exchange: scope refused", limes.CodeInvalidScope, http.StatusBadRequest, "The scope was refused", limes.CategoryDenied}
	// ErrInvalidAuthorizationDetails is authorization_details the exchange
	// will not grant: malformed, or of a type or content it does not
	// understand (RFC 9396 §5).
	ErrInvalidAuthorizationDetails error = &codedError{"exchange: authorization details refused", limes.CodeInvalidAuthorizationDetails, http.StatusBadRequest, "The authorization details were refused", limes.CategoryDenied}
	// ErrUnsupportedGrantType is a token request for another grant.
	ErrUnsupportedGrantType error = &codedError{"exchange: grant type unsupported", limes.CodeUnsupportedGrantType, http.StatusBadRequest, "The grant type is not supported", limes.CategoryInvalid}
)
```

The refusals of an exchange, one per RFC 6749 §5.2 error (and RFC 8707's invalid\_target, RFC 9396's invalid\_authorization\_details) the token endpoint answers with. A Policy refuses with ErrInvalidGrant, ErrInvalidTarget, ErrInvalidScope or ErrInvalidAuthorizationDetails; any other error it returns is the server's, answered as such. Each carries its limes.Code, the status of its problem, a title and its limes.Category, and is registered with limes as the package initialises, so limes.CodeOf, CategoryOf and ProblemOf answer it as the endpoint does, ahead of any limes error it wraps, and limes.Codes lists it: a code added here needs no release of limes.

<sub>[exchange/response.go](../../exchange/response.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.ResourceChallenge"></a>

### exchange.ResourceChallenge

```go
func ResourceChallenge(metadataURL string, scopes []string) string
```

ResourceChallenge is the WWW-Authenticate value an MCP server answers a request that sent no token with: the Bearer scheme, the URL of its resource metadata, and the scopes the request needs, if any (RFC 9728 §5.1, RFC 6750 §3). It names no error, as a request with no credentials gets none (RFC 6750 §3.1); a token the server refused is answered with the verifier's challenges instead, through WithResourceMetadata.

### exchange.WithResourceMetadata

```go
func WithResourceMetadata(resp limes.ErrorResponse, metadataURL string) limes.ErrorResponse
```

WithResourceMetadata is resp, a verifier's answer to a request it refused, with the URL of the resource's metadata added to each challenge (RFC 9728 §5.1): the error codes, the Bearer and DPoP schemes and the algorithms stay the verifier's (RFC 6750 §3, RFC 9449 §7.1). resp is not changed.

```go
type AuthorizationServerMetadata struct {
	// Issuer is its issuer identifier. Required.
	Issuer string `json:"issuer"`
	// TokenEndpoint is the Handler's URL. Required.
	TokenEndpoint string `json:"token_endpoint"`
	// JWKSURI is where the keys of the capabilities it issues are
	// published (jwks.NewHandler).
	JWKSURI string `json:"jwks_uri,omitempty"`
	// GrantTypesSupported is token exchange alone, and
	// ResponseTypesSupported none, there being no authorization endpoint;
	// both are set by the handler.
	GrantTypesSupported    []string `json:"grant_types_supported"`
	ResponseTypesSupported []string `json:"response_types_supported"`
	// TokenEndpointAuthMethodsSupported are how its clients authenticate
	// (HandlerConfig.Authenticate), such as "tls_client_auth".
	TokenEndpointAuthMethodsSupported []string `json:"token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported,omitempty"`
	// DPoPSigningAlgValuesSupported: dpop.SigningAlgorithms when the
	// exchange binds capabilities to keys.
	DPoPSigningAlgValuesSupported []string `json:"dpop_signing_alg_values_supported,omitempty"`
	// AuthorizationDetailsTypesSupported are the RFC 9396 types its policy
	// reads.
	AuthorizationDetailsTypesSupported []string `json:"authorization_details_types_supported,omitempty"`
}
```

AuthorizationServerMetadata is the token exchange's metadata as an authorization server (RFC 8414 §2): one with a token endpoint and no authorization endpoint, issuing nothing but by token exchange.

<sub>[exchange/exchange.go](../../exchange/exchange.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.Config"></a>

### exchange.Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Issuer issues the capabilities. Required. No request to a token
	// endpoint names a tenant, so a store that scopes its rows by tenant
	// must record each capability in its own: with pgstore, give the
	// Issuer pgstore.ScopedIssuance(store).
	Issuer *limes.Issuer
	// Subjects verifies subject tokens. Required.
	Subjects SubjectVerifier
	// Policy decides what each grant issues. Required.
	Policy Policy
	// DPoP checks proofs of possession; nil refuses every request with one.
	DPoP *dpop.Verifier
	// Capabilities verifies a capability given as the subject token, to
	// narrow (Narrow); nil narrows none. CapabilityAudience is the audience
	// such a capability must name: the exchange's own. NarrowPolicy decides
	// each narrowing. All three, or none. A bound capability's proof is
	// checked by Capabilities' own DPoP verifier: give it the nonces of DPoP,
	// so a nonce this endpoint hands out is one that verifier takes.
	Capabilities       *limes.Verifier
	CapabilityAudience string
	NarrowPolicy       NarrowPolicy
	// Exchanges, when set, makes the Exchanger issue one capability per
	// subject token, by its issuer and jti within the tenant the policy
	// names (docs/adr/0009-one-capability-per-subject-token.md): the first
	// exchange issues and records it; every later one, from any replica,
	// hands the same capability back, its token signed again from the
	// record (limes.Issuer.Reissue), so its ceilings are counted once. In
	// this mode a subject token without a jti is refused; an exchange of a
	// capability revoked or expired is refused, never issued anew; one with
	// a proof by another key than the capability is bound to, or none for a
	// bound one, or one for a bearer one, is refused; all with
	// ErrInvalidGrant. One whose audience, as the policy draws it from the
	// targets, is not the capability's is refused with ErrTargetExchanged.
	// A policy that names no TTL gets the subject token's remaining
	// lifetime, not the Issuer's default. The policy still runs on every
	// exchange: it names the tenant. Nil: every exchange issues a capability
	// of its own. The Issuer's store must read records back
	// (limes.RecordReader), as every limes.Store does.
	Exchanges limes.ExchangeStore
	// Now is the clock. Nil: time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
	// Logger logs every exchange and refusal. Nil: slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

Config configures an Exchanger.

### exchange.Decision

```go
type Decision struct {
	// Issue is the capability to issue, held to the grant as Policy says.
	Issue limes.IssueRequest
	// Scopes are the scopes granted, each one the grant asked for: the
	// token response states them as its scope (RFC 6749 §5.1, RFC 8693
	// §2.2.1). Empty grants none: a policy granting every scope asked sets
	// Scopes to Grant.Scopes. A grant that asked for scopes and is granted
	// none is refused with ErrInvalidScope, since a response without scope
	// would state every scope asked. A scope not asked for is the policy's
	// fault, answered as the server's failure. A scope named twice is
	// stated once.
	Scopes []string
}
```

Decision is what a Policy grants: the capability to issue, and the scopes granted.

### exchange.Error

```go
type Error struct {
	// Status is the HTTP status. An invalid_client the endpoint answers
	// 401 with a challenge in the client's scheme, and 400 when the client
	// named none (RFC 9110 §15.5.2).

	// Code is the error code: RFC 6749 §5.2's, RFC 8707's invalid_target,
```

<sub>[exchange/exchange.go](../../exchange/exchange.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.Exchanger.Exchange"></a>

#### exchange.Exchanger.Exchange

```go
func (e *Exchanger) Exchange(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Result, error)
```

Exchange exchanges req's subject token for a capability: it verifies the token and that the client may present it, checks the proof of possession, asks the policy, holds the policy's answer to the request, records the proof and issues. A refusal is one of the errors above, or a dpop error for the proof; every exchange and refusal is logged.

<sub>[exchange/exchange.go](../../exchange/exchange.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.Exchanger.Narrow"></a>

#### exchange.Exchanger.Narrow

```go
func (e *Exchanger) Narrow(ctx context.Context, req NarrowRequest) (Result, error)
```

Narrow exchanges a capability for a narrower one, delegated from it: it verifies the capability as one addressed to the exchange, checks the proof of possession, asks the policy, holds its answer to the request, and delegates. A refusal is one of the errors above, or a dpop error for the proof; every narrowing and refusal is logged.

A bearer capability is narrowed for whichever authenticated client presents it, as it would authorize whoever presents it: unlike Exchange, Narrow does not hold the subject to the client, and Narrowing.Client is the policy's to compare with the parent's ClientID where only the client it was granted to may narrow it. A bound capability is narrowed only with a proof by its key. The child keeps the parent's ClientID, the client the grant began with, unless the policy names another.

<a id="exchange.HandlerConfig"></a>

### exchange.HandlerConfig

```go
type HandlerConfig struct {
	// Exchanger exchanges the tokens. Required.
	Exchanger *Exchanger
	// Authenticate authenticates the client making the request — by mTLS,
	// a client assertion, a shared secret — and names the audiences its
	// subject tokens may be issued for. An error that is or wraps
	// ErrUnauthorizedClient refuses an authenticated client that may not
	// exchange: 400 unauthorized_client. One that is or wraps ErrServerError
	// is the server's failure: 500 server_error, the error logged at ERROR
	// and kept out of the body, so name the client in it. Any other error
	// refuses the client as not authenticated, ErrInvalidClient:
	// invalid_client, 401 with a challenge in the scheme of its
	// Authorization header, or 400 when it sent none (mTLS, a client
	// assertion). Required.
	Authenticate func(r *http.Request) (Client, error)
	// EndpointURL is the token endpoint's URL as clients call it, which
	// their DPoP proofs name (htu). Required when the Exchanger checks DPoP
	// or narrows capabilities (Config.DPoP or Config.Capabilities).
	EndpointURL string
	// MaxBodyBytes bounds the request body the Handler reads. Zero:
	// DefaultMaxBodyBytes; negative is refused. A request whose form the caller parsed already —
	// one /token path serving several grants — is read from r.PostForm, its
	// body left unread, so the caller's own bound is the one that applies;
	// the Handler still checks its content type, and drops empty values
	// from r.PostForm in place.
	MaxBodyBytes int64
	// Logger logs refusals of malformed requests; the Exchanger logs the
	// rest. Nil: slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

HandlerConfig configures a Handler.

<sub>[exchange/handler.go](../../exchange/handler.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.IntrospectionConfig"></a>

### exchange.IntrospectionConfig

```go
type IntrospectionConfig struct {
	// Verifier introspects the tokens: limes.Verifier.IntrospectFor with
	// the client's Audiences, limes.Verifier.Introspect under AnyAudience.
	// Required.
	Verifier *limes.Verifier
	// Authenticate authenticates the resource server or gateway asking, as
	// RFC 7662 §2.1 requires, so the endpoint is no oracle for whoever holds
	// a token. An error that is or wraps ErrUnauthorizedClient refuses one
	// authenticated but not allowed to introspect: 400 unauthorized_client.
	// One that is or wraps ErrServerError is answered 500 server_error, and
	// any other error refuses it as ErrInvalidClient, both as the token
	// endpoint answers them (HandlerConfig.Authenticate). Required.
	Authenticate func(r *http.Request) (Client, error)
	// Audiences are the audiences of the tokens a client may learn about
	// (RFC 7662 §4): a token whose aud names none of them is answered
	// inactive, so one resource server learns nothing of tokens meant for
	// another. Required, unless AnyAudience.
	Audiences func(Client) []string
	// AnyAudience lets any authenticated client learn about any token, its
	// caveats among it: for an endpoint only one resource server, or
	// gateways trusted with every audience, can reach. It excludes
	// Audiences.
	AnyAudience bool
	// MaxBodyBytes bounds the request body. Zero: DefaultMaxBodyBytes;
	// negative is refused.
	MaxBodyBytes int64
	// Logger logs every answer: active at INFO, inactive at WARN with the
	// reason, the server's failures at ERROR, as is a Biscuit copy answered
	// inactive because Verifier does not meter copies. Nil: slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

IntrospectionConfig configures an IntrospectionHandler.

### exchange.NarrowDecision

```go
type NarrowDecision struct {
	// Delegate is the child to delegate, held to the narrowing as
	// NarrowPolicy says.
	Delegate limes.DelegateRequest
	// Scopes are the scopes granted, as Decision.Scopes: each one asked
	// for, none when empty; a narrowing that asked for scopes and is
	// granted none is refused with ErrInvalidScope.
	Scopes []string
}
```

NarrowDecision is what a NarrowPolicy grants: the child to delegate, and the scopes granted.

<sub>[exchange/narrow.go](../../exchange/narrow.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.NarrowPolicy"></a>

### exchange.NarrowPolicy

```go
type NarrowPolicy func(ctx context.Context, n Narrowing) (NarrowDecision, error)
```

NarrowPolicy turns a narrowing into the child to delegate and the scopes granted, or refuses it with ErrInvalidTarget, ErrInvalidScope or ErrInvalidAuthorizationDetails, as a Policy does. The Exchanger sets its DelegateRequest's Parent; its Audience must be drawn from the narrowing's resources and audiences, or be empty to take them all; its ConfirmationJKT must be empty. limes.Issuer.Delegate holds the child to the parent: narrower caveats, an audience within the parent's, an end no later.

<sub>[exchange/narrow.go](../../exchange/narrow.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.NarrowRequest"></a>

### exchange.NarrowRequest

```go
type NarrowRequest struct {
	// Client is the client asking; its ID is required, for the log and as
	// its share of the DPoP replay cache.
	Client Client
	// SubjectToken is the capability narrowed. Required.
	SubjectToken string
	// Resources and Audiences are what the child is asked for; at least one
	// of either, each within the parent's audience. Each resource is an
	// absolute URI without a fragment, else refused with ErrInvalidTarget.
	Resources, Audiences []string
	// Scopes and AuthorizationDetails are handed to the policy.
	Scopes               []string
	AuthorizationDetails json.RawMessage
	// DPoP is the request's proof. For a parent bound to a key it is the
	// proof of holding it, over the subject token, and the child keeps the
	// binding; for an unbound parent, a token request's proof (RFC 9449 §5)
	// binds the child to its key, and none leaves the child a bearer one.
	DPoP dpop.Proof
}
```

NarrowRequest is an exchange of a capability for a narrower one, for a sub-agent: the capability is the subject token (RFC 8693 §2.1), of type IssuedTokenTypeCapability.

<sub>[exchange/narrow.go](../../exchange/narrow.go)</sub>

### exchange.Narrowing

```go
type Narrowing struct {
	Parent               limes.VerifiedCapability
	Client               Client
	Resources, Audiences []string
	Scopes               []string
	AuthorizationDetails json.RawMessage
}
```

Narrowing is what a NarrowPolicy decides on: the verified parent, its client, and what is asked for.

<sub>[exchange/narrow.go](../../exchange/narrow.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.Policy"></a>

### exchange.Policy

```go
type Policy func(ctx context.Context, g Grant) (Decision, error)
```

Policy turns a grant into the capability to issue and the scopes granted, or refuses it with ErrInvalidGrant, ErrInvalidTarget, ErrInvalidScope or ErrInvalidAuthorizationDetails. It refuses authorization\_details of a type it does not understand (RFC 9396 §5). In its Decision.Issue, Audience must be drawn from the grant's resources and audiences, or be empty to take them all; ConfirmationJKT must be empty, the Exchanger setting it from the proof; SubjectIssuer, when set, must be the subject token's issuer, and OnBehalfOf, when set, must name its subject; an empty SubjectIssuer, Session or ClientID takes the subject token's. TTL, the Issuer's default when zero (limes.Issuer.DefaultTTL; the subject token's remaining lifetime under Config.Exchanges), is capped at the subject token's remaining lifetime. A Decision.Issue breaking these is the policy's fault, answered as the server's failure. Nothing is granted that the policy did not choose: there is no default policy. A subject token may be exchanged again and again until it expires, each exchange issuing a capability of its own, with ceilings of its own, unless Config.Exchanges issues one capability per subject token: a policy that grants a budget per user, not per exchange, keys it on Grant.Subject (its Issuer and Subject). Set both ceilings explicitly: Caveats.Requests to a Max or Unlimited, since Issue refuses a capability no request can use and the exchange answers that as the server's failure; Caveats.Budget to what it may spend, the zero budget being none.

<sub>[exchange/exchange.go](../../exchange/exchange.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.Request"></a>

### exchange.Request

```go
type Request struct {
	Client Client
	// SubjectToken is the token exchanged. Required.
	SubjectToken string
	// Resources are the RFC 8707 resources, and Audiences the RFC 8693
	// audiences, the capability is asked for. At least one of either; the
	// capability's audience is drawn from them. Each resource is an
	// absolute URI without a fragment, else refused with ErrInvalidTarget.
	Resources, Audiences []string
	// Scopes are the scopes asked for.
	Scopes []string
	// AuthorizationDetails is the RFC 9396 authorization_details, a JSON
	// array as sent; nil for none. The policy reads it.
	AuthorizationDetails json.RawMessage
	// DPoP is the request's proof of possession, binding the capability to
	// its key (RFC 9449 §5); a zero Proof issues a bearer capability.
	DPoP dpop.Proof
}
```

Request is an exchange: the subject token, and what is asked for in exchange (RFC 8693 §2.1).

<sub>[exchange/exchange.go](../../exchange/exchange.go)</sub>
<a id="exchange.ResourceMetadata"></a>

### exchange.ResourceMetadata

```go
type ResourceMetadata struct {
	// Resource is the resource's identifier, the URL its clients name in
	// `resource` (RFC 8707). Required.
	Resource string `json:"resource"`
	// AuthorizationServers are the issuers its tokens come from: an MCP
	// client discovers its authorization server here. Required.
	AuthorizationServers []string `json:"authorization_servers"`
	// ScopesSupported are the scopes a client may ask for.
	ScopesSupported []string `json:"scopes_supported,omitempty"`
	// BearerMethodsSupported are how a token is presented. Empty:
	// BearerMethodHeader alone.
	BearerMethodsSupported []string `json:"bearer_methods_supported,omitempty"`
	// ResourceName and ResourceDocumentation describe it to people.
	ResourceName          string `json:"resource_name,omitempty"`
	ResourceDocumentation string `json:"resource_documentation,omitempty"`
	// DPoPSigningAlgValuesSupported are the algorithms its DPoP proofs may
	// use (RFC 9449 §5.1): dpop.SigningAlgorithms when it checks them.
	DPoPSigningAlgValuesSupported []string `json:"dpop_signing_alg_values_supported,omitempty"`
	// DPoPBoundAccessTokensRequired says it accepts only DPoP-bound tokens.
	DPoPBoundAccessTokensRequired bool `json:"dpop_bound_access_tokens_required,omitempty"`
}
```

ResourceMetadata is a protected resource's metadata (RFC 9728 §2), which an MCP server must publish: where its clients get tokens, and how they present them.

<a id="exchange.Subject"></a>

### exchange.Subject

```go
type Subject struct {
	// Issuer and Subject are the token's iss and sub. The Exchanger
	// records Issuer beside the capability (limes.IssueRequest.SubjectIssuer),
	// so a bulk revocation by ClientID or SessionID names the identity
	// provider that issued them (limes.BulkRevoker).
	Issuer, Subject string
	// ClientID is the client the token was issued to.
	ClientID string
	// Audience is the token's aud: the resources it was issued for.
	Audience []string
	// Scopes are the token's scope, split at spaces.
	Scopes []string
	// ID is the token's jti.
	ID string
	// IssuedAt and ExpiresAt are its iat and exp.
	IssuedAt, ExpiresAt time.Time
	// JKT is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the key the token is bound to
	// (RFC 9449 cnf.jkt); empty for a bearer token.
	JKT string
	// SessionID is the identity provider's session the token was issued
	// in, its sid (OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout §2.4); empty for none.
	// The Exchanger records it beside the capability
	// (limes.IssueRequest.Session), so ending the session revokes what was
	// exchanged in it (limes.BulkRevoker).
	SessionID string
	// Claims are all of the token's claims, for a policy that reads one of
	// its identity provider's own, such as an organisation. It is also where
	// a multi-tenant SubjectVerifier puts the tenant it resolved, under a
	// key of its own, for the Policy to check and to set as the issued
	// capability's Subject.TenantID: Subject names no tenant itself.
	Claims map[string]any
}
```

Subject is a subject token a SubjectVerifier accepted: who it names, for which client, and until when.

<a id="jwtverify"></a><a id="package-jwtverify"></a>

## Package jwtverify

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/exchange/jwtverify"`

Package jwtverify verifies JWT access tokens (RFC 9068) as an exchange.SubjectVerifier, through jwx: the library that implements the format, as no identity provider's SDK covers every provider. It is a package of its own so that package exchange links no JOSE library for a consumer that verifies subject tokens on a stack of its own (docs/adr/0010-exchange-jose-subpackage.md).

<a id="jwtverify.TypeAccessToken"></a><a id="jwtverify.TypeAccessTokenMedia"></a><a id="jwtverify.ClaimClientID"></a>

### jwtverify.TypeAccessToken, jwtverify.TypeAccessTokenMedia, jwtverify.ClaimClientID

```go
const (
	TypeAccessToken      = "at+jwt"
	TypeAccessTokenMedia = "application/at+jwt"

	// ClaimClientID is the claim RFC 9068 names the client in.
	ClaimClientID = "client_id"
)
```

The JWT access token profile (RFC 9068): the types §2.1 gives the header, and the claims §2.2 requires.

<sub>[exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go](../../exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go)</sub>
<a id="jwtverify.DefaultAlgorithms"></a>

### jwtverify.DefaultAlgorithms

```go
func DefaultAlgorithms() []string
```

DefaultAlgorithms are the asymmetric JWS algorithms a Verifier accepts when its config names none, and the only ones a config may name. A symmetric one would let anyone holding the key, the identity provider's other clients among them, mint tokens. Each call returns a fresh slice: changing it widens no Verifier's allow-list.

<sub>[exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go](../../exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go)</sub>
<a id="jwtverify.Config"></a>

### jwtverify.Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Issuer is the identity provider's issuer identifier, which a token's
	// iss must equal. Required.
	Issuer string
	// Keys are the identity provider's public keys: RemoteKeys over its JWKS
	// URL keeps them fresh. Required.
	Keys *KeySource
	// Types are the header types accepted, compared without regard to case.
	// Empty: TypeAccessToken and TypeAccessTokenMedia, as RFC 9068 requires.
	// A provider that types its access tokens otherwise ("JWT") is accepted
	// only by naming its type here.
	Types []string
	// ClientIDClaim is the claim naming the client. Empty: ClaimClientID.
	// A provider that names it elsewhere ("azp") is read by naming it here.
	ClientIDClaim string
	// Algorithms are the JWS algorithms accepted. Empty: DefaultAlgorithms().
	Algorithms []string
	// ClockSkew is how far exp, nbf and iat may be off the clock: the
	// identity provider's clock is not the verifier's. Zero:
	// limes.DefaultLeeway, the skew a limes verifier allows a capability's
	// times; negative is refused.
	ClockSkew time.Duration
	// NoClockSkew holds exp, nbf and iat to the clock exactly, for an
	// identity provider that shares it. It excludes a ClockSkew.
	NoClockSkew bool
	// Now is the clock. Nil: time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
}
```

Config configures a Verifier.

<sub>[exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go](../../exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go)</sub>
<a id="jwtverify.KeySource"></a>

### jwtverify.KeySource

```go
type KeySource struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

KeySource gives the identity provider's current public keys, or an error when it has none to give: its JWKS out of reach and never fetched. That is the server's failure, answered as one, never a refusal of the token. StaticKeys and RemoteKeys make one. It names no type of the JOSE library the verifier reads keys with, so that library can change major version without changing this package's API.

<sub>[exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go](../../exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go)</sub>
<a id="jwtverify.RemoteKeys"></a>

#### jwtverify.RemoteKeys

```go
func RemoteKeys(ctx context.Context, rawURL string, client *http.Client) (*KeySource, error)
```

RemoteKeys is a KeySource of the JWK Set at rawURL, fetched in the background every few minutes until ctx is done. rawURL must be an https URL with a host: over anything else whoever sits on the path chooses the keys, and so the subject tokens the exchange accepts; any other is limes.ErrInvalidConfig. client fetches it; nil: a client bounded by jwks.DefaultFetchTimeout, as jwks.Remote's. Whatever the client's own redirect policy, a redirect to another scheme or host is refused, on a copy of the client: the caller's is left as it is. It does not wait for the first fetch. A token naming a kid the set does not hold, or arriving while no usable set is held, fetches it again at once, at most once per jwks.DefaultMinRefreshInterval. While the last fetch failed, with none succeeding since, such a kid is an error wrapping jwks.ErrUnavailable rather than a refused token: it may be a key rotated in meanwhile. The last set fetched is served while rawURL is out of reach, for at most jwks.DefaultMaxStale; never fetched or past that, the keys are an error wrapping jwks.ErrUnavailable, the server's. Fetches a token starts, and every failed fetch, are logged to slog.Default().

<sub>[exchange/jwtverify/remote.go](../../exchange/jwtverify/remote.go)</sub>
<a id="jwtverify.StaticKeys"></a>

#### jwtverify.StaticKeys

```go
func StaticKeys(jwks []byte) (*KeySource, error)
```

StaticKeys is a KeySource of the fixed key set jwks, a JWK Set document (RFC 7517 §5). A document that is no JWK Set is refused with limes.ErrInvalidConfig.

Verifier is the exchange.SubjectVerifier for JWT access tokens (RFC 9068), verified through jwx: the library that implements the format, as no identity provider's SDK covers every provider.

<sub>[exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go](../../exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go)</sub>

```go
func New(cfg Config) (*Verifier, error)
```

<sub>[exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go](../../exchange/jwtverify/jwtverify.go)</sub>
<a id="jwtverify.Verifier.VerifySubject"></a>

#### jwtverify.Verifier.VerifySubject

```go
func (v *Verifier) VerifySubject(ctx context.Context, token string) (exchange.Subject, error)
```

VerifySubject verifies token as an RFC 9068 access token of the configured issuer: its type and algorithm, its signature under the issuer's keys (the key its kid names, which it must name), its lifetime, and every claim the profile requires. A token it refuses is exchange.ErrInvalidGrant; keys it cannot get are another error, the server's.
